About this document

This document provides the teaching content for Spatial and Product Design Years
11–13 of the New Zealand Curriculum. Equivalent for Te Marautanga o Aotearoa is
being published separately.

Progress and assessment information for Spatial and Product Design Years 11–13 is
still in development. Once that is completed, Spatial and Product Design Years 11–13
is proposed to be made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum
Statement under section 90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Spatial and Product Design Years 11–13 will be required to start using it in
Year 11 from 1 January 2028, in Year 12 from 1 January 2029, and in Year 13 from 1
January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.




Spatial and Product Design | Years 11-13 | October 2026                                  Page 2

  In Spatial and Product Design, students are taught how products, spaces and
  environments are designed to respond to user needs and aspirations. Students
  are taught how to apply design thinking and structured design processes using
  concepts and practices such as visual communication, user-centred design,
  design heritage and design evaluation to develop innovative design outcomes.

Through the study of Spatial and Product Design, students are taught how design
outcomes emerge from the interaction of people, materials, environments, and ideas.
They are taught to analyse and respond to design opportunities using creative and
critical thinking, while considering how cultural, social, environmental, and contextual
factors influence design decisions and outcomes.

Spatial and Product Design provides students with the knowledge and practices to
represent, analyse, synthesise, evaluate and apply design concepts within spatial and
product-based contexts. Through iterative and interdisciplinary design processes,
students generate, model, test, and refine solutions using visual and written
communication, drawing systems, modelling, and prototyping to create purposeful
and responsive outcomes.

As students progress through Years 11–13, they are taught to engage in increasingly
sophisticated design practices that involve evaluating alternatives, managing
complexity, and refining ideas through informed decision-making. They learn to use
feedback, testing, and iteration to improve design outcomes, and to work with users,
communities and others affected by design decisions to develop meaningful and
responsible design solutions.

  Spatial and Product Design leads to pathways in architecture, industrial and
  product design, interior and spatial design, engineering and related creative and
  technological disciplines.
